gg_crosshair <- function(xint = 0, yint = 0, lty = 2) {
  if (!is.null(xint)) gv = geom_vline(xintercept = xint, linetype = lty)
  else gv = NULL
  if (!is.null(yint)) gh = geom_hline(yintercept = yint, linetype = lty)
  else gh = NULL
  
  list(gv, gh)
}



randstring <- function(n = 5000) {
  a <- do.call(paste0, replicate(5, sample(LETTERS, n, TRUE), FALSE))
  paste0(a, sprintf("%04d", sample(9999, n, TRUE)), sample(LETTERS, n, TRUE))
}

#| label: load_data
data_list <- list()
study_uid <- Sys.getenv('JATOS_COLORS_AND_IMAGERY_STUDY_2026H_UID')

temp_dir <- tempdir(check = T)
temp_dir <- gsub('\\\\', '/', temp_dir)
temp_dir <- paste(temp_dir, randstring(1), sep = '/')

metadata <- read_jatos_export(study_uid, temp_dir)

finished_study_ids <- metadata[metadata$studyState == 'FINISHED', c('id', "endDate", "startDate")]
setDT(finished_study_ids)
finished_study_ids[,id:=as.character(id)]
finished_study_ids[,endDate:=as.POSIXct(endDate/1000, origin="1970-01-01")]
finished_study_ids[,startDate:=as.POSIXct(startDate/1000, origin="1970-01-01")]
finished_study_ids <- finished_study_ids[!is.na(endDate)] 
finished_study_ids <- filter_jatos_start_date(finished_study_ids)
finished_study <- copy(finished_study_ids)

comp_res_meta <- rbindlist(lapply(1:length(metadata$componentResults), \(x) {
  dt <- as.data.table(metadata$componentResults[[x]])
  dt
}), fill = T)

flist <- list.files(temp_dir, '*.txt', full.names = T, recursive = T)
flist <- flist[str_extract(flist,'study_result_(\\d+)', group = 1)%in%finished_study_ids$id]
# Select the last finished attempt of each component within each study session.
component_files <- merge(data.table(
  file = flist,
  participant = str_extract(flist, 'study_result_(\\d+)', group = 1),
  result_id = str_extract(flist, 'comp-result_(\\d+)', group = 1)),
  comp_res_meta[, .(result_id = as.character(id), componentId, componentState, endDate)],
  by = 'result_id')
component_files <- component_files[componentState == 'FINISHED'][order(endDate), .SD[.N],
  by = .(participant, componentId)]
flist_vviq <- component_files[componentId == 49456, file]
flist_afterimage <- component_files[componentId == 49460, file]
flist_colors <- component_files[componentId %in% c(49458, 49459), file]

data_vviq <- rbindlist(lapply(c(flist_vviq), \(x){
  data <- read_json(x)
  responses <- unlist(lapply(data, \(trial) {
    if (is.list(trial$response) && length(trial$response) == 4L) trial$response
  }))
  data.table(participant = str_extract(x, 'study_result_(\\d+)', group = 1),
             result_id=str_extract(x, 'comp-result_(\\d+)', group = 1),
             vviq = if (length(responses) == 16L) sum(responses) else NA_real_)
}))

data_afterimage <- rbindlist(lapply(flist_afterimage, \(x) {
  rating <- Filter(\(trial) isTRUE(trial$ai_run == 2) &&
    identical(trial$ai_page, 'relative_rating'), read_json(x))
  stopifnot(length(rating) == 1L, rating[[1]]$ai_code %in% -2:3)
  data.table(participant = str_extract(x, 'study_result_(\\d+)', group = 1),
    afterimage_relative = if (rating[[1]]$ai_code == 3) NA_real_ else rating[[1]]$ai_code)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(data_afterimage$participant))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(data_vviq$participant))
data_vviq <- merge(finished_study_ids[, .(participant = id)], data_vviq,
  by = 'participant', all.x = TRUE)
data_vviq <- merge(data_vviq, data_afterimage, by = 'participant', all.x = TRUE)
stopifnot(nrow(data_vviq) == nrow(finished_study_ids))

data_color <- suppressWarnings(rbindlist(lapply(c(flist_colors), \(x){
  # print(x)
  comp_res_id <- str_extract(x, '(?<=comp-result_)\\d{6}')
  data <- read_json(x)
  if (length(data)<10){
    return(data.frame())
  }
  data <- data[sapply(data, \(x) x$trial_type=='psychophysics')]
  data <- rbindlist(data, fill = T)
  if ('score' %nin% colnames(data)){
    return(data.frame())
  }

    
  data[,score:=as.numeric(score)]
  data[!is.na(left_colors), left_sd:=circ_sd_360(as.numeric(str_split(left_colors,',', simplify = T))), by = left_colors]
  data[!is.na(right_colors), right_sd:=circ_sd_360(as.numeric(str_split(right_colors,',', simplify = T))), by = right_colors]
  data[,left_colors:=NULL]
  data[,right_colors:=NULL]
  setnafill(data, type = "locf",cols = c('target_color','distr_color','left_color','right_color','target_sd', 'distr_sd', 'target_x', 'distr_x', 'similarity_bin', 'color_bin','left_sd','right_sd','cue_pos','cued_color','cue_n','rt'))
  setnafill(data, type = "nocb", cols = c('score'))
  data<-data[trial_type=='psychophysics'&seq_type=='response']

  data[,participant:=str_extract(x, 'study_result_(\\d+)', group = 1)]
  data[,result_id:=str_extract(x, 'comp-result_(\\d+)', group = 1)]
  data <- merge(data, finished_study_ids, by.x = 'participant', by.y = 'id')
  
  data
  
}), fill = T))

unlink(paste0(temp_dir, "/*"))

data_vviq <- data_vviq[participant%in%finished_study$id]

# Instructions

Read the report and use it as a basis for your presentation. You can also download the preprocessed data from `colors_and_imagery.csv` and use your favorite software (JASP, jamovi, R, SPSS) to analyze it to get more insight into the study results. The data file has the following columns:

* `participant` - participant identifier (factor with levels "S1", "S2", etc.)
* `vviq` - Visual Vividness Imagery Questionnaire sum (0–64; higher scores indicate more vivid imagery)
* `afterimage_relative` - second-run imagery/afterimage comparison (−2 to +2; higher means stronger imagery relative to the afterimage; unsure is missing)
* `block` - block number (0 = training, 1-2 = main experimental blocks)
* `trial_number` - trial number within the experiment
* `similarity_bin` - angular distance between target and distractor colors in degrees (20°, 45°, or 135°)
* `target_color` - the target color value in degrees (0-360°)
* `distr_color` - the distractor color value in degrees (0-360°)
* `td_dist` - difference between target and distractor colors in degrees
* `left_color` - color value of the left stimulus in degrees
* `right_color` - color value of the right stimulus in degrees
* `target_noise` - noise level of the target stimulus (factor: "low" or "high")
* `distr_noise` - noise level of the distractor stimulus (factor: "low" or "high")
* `target_x` - x-coordinate of the target position (-300 for left, 300 for right)
* `distr_x` - x-coordinate of the distractor position (-300 for left, 300 for right)
* `cue_n` - cue number (1 = first report, 2 = second report)
* `cue_pos` - position of the cue (-300 for left, 300 for right)
* `cued_color` - the color value that was cued (the one to be reported) in degrees
* `resp_color` - the color value reported by the participant in degrees
* `error` - angular deviation between the target color and response color in degrees
* `abs_err` - absolute value of the error in degrees
* `noise` - combined noise condition from target and distractor (factor with 4 levels: "low - low", "high - low", "low - high", "high - high")
* `be_c` - error after correction for individual biases (more reliable measure than raw error)
* `is_outlier` - a boolean indicating whether the trial is an outlier to be excluded
* `abs_be_c` - absolute value of the bias-corrected error
* `bias_to_distr_raw` - raw bias toward the distractor in degrees
* `bias_to_distr_corr` - bias-corrected bias toward the distractor in degrees

## Participants
`r str_to_sentence(xfun::numbers_to_words(finished_study[,.N]))` participants took part in the study. `r str_to_sentence(xfun::numbers_to_words(finished_study[,.N]-data_color[,lengthu(participant)]))` participants were excluded under the existing memory-quality rules (circular SD of errors above 60 deg. or fewer than 250 main-task report rows).

# Results

```{r}
#| label: imagery-participant-metrics
data_color_accuracy <- data_color[is_outlier == FALSE]
data_color_accuracy[, cue_n := factor(cue_n, levels = 1:2)]
memory_metrics <- data_color_accuracy[,
  .(memory_mae = mean(abs_be_c), n_memory_reports = .N), by = participant]
imagery_metrics <- merge(data_vviq, memory_metrics, by = 'participant', all.x = TRUE)
stopifnot(nrow(imagery_metrics) == nrow(finished_study_ids),
  !anyDuplicated(imagery_metrics$participant),
  all(is.na(imagery_metrics$vviq) | imagery_metrics$vviq %between% c(0, 64)),
  all(is.na(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative) | imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative %in% -2:2))

correlation_specs <- data.table(
  x = c('vviq', 'vviq', 'afterimage_relative'),
  y = c('afterimage_relative', 'memory_mae', 'memory_mae'),
  comparison = c('VVIQ – imagery/afterimage', 'VVIQ – memory MAE', 'Imagery/afterimage – memory MAE'),
  method = c('spearman', 'pearson', 'spearman'))
imagery_correlations <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(correlation_specs)), function(i) {
  spec <- correlation_specs[i]
  pairs <- imagery_metrics[is.finite(get(spec$x)) & is.finite(get(spec$y))]
  test <- if (nrow(pairs) >= 3L && uniqueN(pairs[[spec$x]]) > 1L && uniqueN(pairs[[spec$y]]) > 1L)
    cor.test(pairs[[spec$x]], pairs[[spec$y]], method = spec$method, exact = FALSE) else NULL
  data.table(comparison = spec$comparison, method = spec$method, n = nrow(pairs),
    estimate = if (is.null(test)) NA_real_ else unname(test$estimate),
    p = if (is.null(test)) NA_real_ else test$p.value)
}))
fwrite(imagery_correlations, 'imagery_correlations.csv')
```

```{r}
#| label: imagery-condition-effects
condition_accuracy <- data_color_accuracy[, .(mae = mean(abs_be_c)),
  by = .(participant, target_noise, distr_noise, similarity_bin, cue_n)]
stopifnot(nrow(condition_accuracy) == uniqueN(data_color_accuracy$participant) * 24L)

target_accuracy <- dcast(condition_accuracy, participant ~ target_noise,
  value.var = 'mae', fun.aggregate = mean)
noise_changes <- target_accuracy[, .(participant, effect = 'target_noise', change = high - low)]
report_accuracy <- dcast(condition_accuracy, participant ~ cue_n,
  value.var = 'mae', fun.aggregate = mean)
report_changes <- report_accuracy[, .(participant, effect = 'report_order', change = `2` - `1`)]
condition_effects <- merge(rbind(noise_changes, report_changes),
  imagery_metrics[, .(participant, vviq, afterimage_relative)], by = 'participant', all.x = TRUE)
stopifnot(nrow(condition_effects) == uniqueN(data_color_accuracy$participant) * 2L,
  !anyDuplicated(condition_effects[, .(participant, effect)]))
fwrite(condition_effects, 'imagery_condition_effects.csv')
effects_wide <- dcast(condition_effects, participant ~ effect, value.var = 'change')
setnames(effects_wide, c('target_noise', 'report_order'),
  c('target_noise_cost', 'report_order_cost'))
imagery_metrics <- merge(imagery_metrics, effects_wide, by = 'participant', all.x = TRUE)
fwrite(imagery_metrics, 'imagery_participant_metrics.csv')

effect_specs <- CJ(effect = c('target_noise', 'report_order'),
  measure = c('vviq', 'afterimage_relative'))
effect_correlations <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(effect_specs)), function(i) {
  spec <- effect_specs[i]
  pairs <- condition_effects[effect == spec$effect & is.finite(get(spec$measure))]
  method <- if (spec$measure == 'vviq') 'pearson' else 'spearman'
  test <- if (nrow(pairs) >= 3L && uniqueN(pairs[[spec$measure]]) > 1L && uniqueN(pairs$change) > 1L)
    cor.test(pairs[[spec$measure]], pairs$change, method = method, exact = FALSE) else NULL
  data.table(effect = spec$effect, measure = spec$measure, method, n = nrow(pairs),
    estimate = if (is.null(test)) NA_real_ else unname(test$estimate),
    p = if (is.null(test)) NA_real_ else test$p.value)
}))
effect_correlations[, p_holm := p.adjust(p, method = 'holm')]
fwrite(effect_correlations, 'imagery_effect_correlations.csv')

effect_labels <- c(target_noise = 'Noise in the target',
  report_order = 'Second report minus first')
measure_labels <- c(vviq = 'VVIQ', afterimage_relative = 'Imagery / afterimage')
effect_pairs <- melt(condition_effects,
  id.vars = c('participant', 'effect', 'change'),
  measure.vars = c('vviq', 'afterimage_relative'),
  variable.name = 'measure', value.name = 'imagery')

report_order_test <- t.test(report_changes$change, mu = 0)
```

## Imagery and memory scores

```{r}
#| label: fig-vviq
#| fig-cap: "Distributions of VVIQ scores, imagery/afterimage ratings and memory mean absolute error (MAE). Each dot represents one participant with that measure available. Higher imagery scores indicate stronger imagery; lower MAE indicates better memory."
#| fig-asp: 0.85

score_labels <- c(vviq = 'VVIQ score',
  afterimage_relative = 'Imagery / afterimage rating', memory_mae = 'Memory MAE (degrees)')
score_dot_sizes <- c(vviq = 1, afterimage_relative = 0.08, memory_mae = 0.3)
score_distributions <- lapply(names(score_labels), function(measure) {
  ggplot(imagery_metrics[is.finite(get(measure))], aes(x = .data[[measure]])) +
    geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, dotsize = score_dot_sizes[[measure]]) +
    labs(x = score_labels[[measure]]) +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
})
score_distributions[[1]] <- score_distributions[[1]] + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 64))
score_distributions[[2]] <- score_distributions[[2]] +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = -2:2, limits = c(-2.5, 2.5))
patchwork::wrap_plots(score_distributions, ncol = 1)
```

The VVIQ scores were between `r min(data_vviq$vviq, na.rm = TRUE)` and `r max(data_vviq$vviq, na.rm = TRUE)` (`r apa_mean_conf(data_vviq$vviq)`). Questionnaire scores are missing for `r sum(is.na(data_vviq$vviq))` sessions without all 16 saved questionnaire responses; a missing questionnaire score does not by itself exclude a session from the memory analyses.

The imagery/afterimage ratings ranged from `r min(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative, na.rm = TRUE)` to `r max(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative, na.rm = TRUE)`, with a median of `r median(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative, na.rm = TRUE)` across `r sum(is.finite(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative))` participants. `r sum(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative < 0, na.rm = TRUE)` rated their imagery as weaker than the afterimage, `r sum(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative == 0, na.rm = TRUE)` as similar, and `r sum(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative > 0, na.rm = TRUE)` as stronger. The rating was missing or unsure for `r sum(is.na(imagery_metrics$afterimage_relative))` session(s). Only the second run was analyzed; the first was practice.

Memory MAE ranged from `r f_round(min(imagery_metrics$memory_mae, na.rm = TRUE))` to `r f_round(max(imagery_metrics$memory_mae, na.rm = TRUE))` degrees across `r sum(is.finite(imagery_metrics$memory_mae))` participants, with an average of `r apa_mean_conf(imagery_metrics$memory_mae)` degrees (95% confidence interval in brackets). Lower MAE indicates more accurate memory. These scores use the same outlier exclusions and hue-bias correction as the accuracy analyses below.

## Color recall accuracy

The data were preprocessed to exclude outliers and correct systematic response biases for different hues.

```{r}
#| label: fig-noise-effect
#| fig-cap: "Effect of target and distractor noise on color recall accuracy, shown separately for the first and second reports. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals corrected for within-subject comparisons."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-asp: 0.5

plot_pointrange(data_color_accuracy, aes(x = target_noise, 
                               y = abs_be_c, 
                               color = distr_noise),
               within_subj = TRUE, 
               wid = 'participant', 
               withinvars = c('target_noise', 'distr_noise', 'cue_n')) +
  facet_wrap(~cue_n, labeller = as_labeller(c('1' = 'First report', '2' = 'Second report'))) +
  labs(x = 'Target noise level', 
       y = 'Average absolute error (degrees)',
       color = 'Distractor noise') +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = c("Low", "High")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Low", "High")) 

# Run ANOVA
ez_res_abs_err <- ezANOVA(
  data = data_color_accuracy,
  dv = .(abs_be_c),
  wid = .(participant),
  within = .(target_noise, distr_noise, cue_n),
  type = 3
)
```

A three-way repeated-measures ANOVA tested target noise, distractor noise and report order, including all their interactions. The results are summarized below.

```{r}
#| label: noise-order-anova-results
#| results: asis
anova_effect_labels <- c(target_noise = 'Target noise', distr_noise = 'Distractor noise',
  cue_n = 'Report order', `target_noise:distr_noise` = 'Target noise × distractor noise',
  `target_noise:cue_n` = 'Target noise × report order',
  `distr_noise:cue_n` = 'Distractor noise × report order',
  `target_noise:distr_noise:cue_n` = 'Target noise × distractor noise × report order')
stopifnot(setequal(ez_res_abs_err$ANOVA$Effect, names(anova_effect_labels)))
knitr::kable(data.table(
  Effect = unname(anova_effect_labels[ez_res_abs_err$ANOVA$Effect]),
  Statistics = vapply(ez_res_abs_err$ANOVA$Effect,
    function(effect) apa(ez_res_abs_err, effect), character(1))))
```

Errors were larger for high-noise targets and for the second report, showing clear effects of target noise and report order. There was no clear overall effect of distractor noise, and none of the two-way interactions reached p < .05. However, the three-way interaction showed that the combined effect of target and distractor noise differed between the first and second reports. The panels in @fig-noise-effect therefore need to be considered separately rather than relying only on effects averaged across reports.

```{r}
#| label: imagery-report-order-tests
noise_order_accuracy <- data_color_accuracy[, .(mae = mean(abs_be_c)),
  by = .(participant, target_noise, distr_noise, cue_n)]
order_wide <- dcast(noise_order_accuracy, participant + target_noise + distr_noise ~ cue_n,
  value.var = 'mae')
order_differences <- rbind(
  order_wide[, .(participant, comparison = paste('Target', target_noise, '/ distractor', distr_noise),
    change = `2` - `1`)],
  order_wide[, .(comparison = 'All noise conditions', change = mean(`2` - `1`)), by = participant])
order_tests <- order_differences[, {
  test <- t.test(change)
  .(n = .N, mean_change = mean(change), summary = apa_mean_conf(change),
    statistics = apa(test), p = test$p.value)
}, by = comparison]
order_tests[, p_holm := p.adjust(p, method = 'holm')]
```

Paired comparisons tested the second minus first report, both overall and within each combination of target and distractor noise. Positive differences mean that the second report was less accurate. The five p-values were adjusted together using Holm's method.

```{r}
#| results: asis
knitr::kable(order_tests[, .(Comparison = comparison, N = n,
  `Second minus first (degrees; 95% CI)` = summary, Test = statistics,
  `Holm-adjusted p` = vapply(p_holm, round_p, character(1), include.rel = FALSE))])
```

Across the four noise conditions, the second-report cost was `r order_tests[comparison == 'All noise conditions', summary]` degrees. `r if (all(order_tests[comparison != 'All noise conditions', p_holm] < .05)) 'The second report was less accurate in all four noise combinations after adjustment.' else 'The adjusted comparisons show which noise combinations provided clear evidence for a second-report cost.'` These comparisons describe the report-order differences; the three-way interaction above tests whether the noise effects themselves change with report order.

## How are the two imagery measures related?

We compared VVIQ scores with the second-run imagery/afterimage rating (@fig-imagery-measures). Higher values on both measures indicate stronger imagery, although one is a questionnaire and the other compares imagery with an afterimage. We used Spearman's correlation because the afterimage rating has five ordered categories.

```{r}
#| label: imagery-question-tables
#| results: asis
correlation_table <- function(stats) knitr::kable(stats[, .(Comparison = comparison,
  Method = ifelse(method == 'spearman', 'Spearman rho', 'Pearson r'), N = n,
  Correlation = round(estimate, 3), p = vapply(p, round_p, character(1), include.rel = FALSE))])
correlation_table(imagery_correlations[comparison == 'VVIQ – imagery/afterimage'])
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-imagery-measures
#| fig-cap: "VVIQ scores and imagery/afterimage ratings. Each point is one participant with both scores; vertical jitter separates overlapping ordinal ratings. The line and 95% confidence band are a descriptive linear fit; the test uses Spearman's correlation on the original ratings."
#| fig-asp: 0.6

ggplot(imagery_metrics[is.finite(vviq) & is.finite(afterimage_relative)],
  aes(x = vviq, y = afterimage_relative)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.07, seed = 20261110),
    colour = default_colors[1], alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = TRUE, colour = 'black') +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = -2:2) +
  labs(x = 'VVIQ score', y = 'Imagery / afterimage rating')
```

`r if (imagery_correlations[comparison == 'VVIQ – imagery/afterimage', p] < .05) 'Higher questionnaire scores were associated with stronger imagery relative to the afterimage.' else 'The data did not show a clear association between the questionnaire and imagery/afterimage rating.'` This comparison uses `r imagery_correlations[comparison == 'VVIQ – imagery/afterimage', n]` participants with both scores, including those excluded only from the memory analyses.

## Does imagery ability predict overall color memory performance?

We related each imagery measure to the participant's memory MAE (@fig-imagery-memory). A negative correlation would mean that stronger imagery was associated with more accurate memory. VVIQ associations use Pearson's correlation; imagery/afterimage associations use Spearman's correlation. Each test uses participants with both of its measures available.

```{r}
#| results: asis
correlation_table(imagery_correlations[comparison != 'VVIQ – imagery/afterimage'])
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-imagery-memory
#| fig-cap: "Imagery measures and overall memory MAE. Each point is one participant with both measures available. Lower MAE means better memory. Lines and 95% confidence bands show descriptive linear fits, including for the ordinal afterimage rating."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-asp: 0.4

measure_labels <- c(vviq = 'VVIQ', afterimage_relative = 'Imagery / afterimage')
imagery_memory_pairs <- melt(imagery_metrics, id.vars = c('participant', 'memory_mae'),
  measure.vars = names(measure_labels), variable.name = 'measure', value.name = 'imagery')
imagery_association_plot <- ggplot(imagery_memory_pairs[is.finite(imagery) & is.finite(memory_mae)],
  aes(x = imagery, y = memory_mae)) +
  geom_point(colour = default_colors[1], alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = TRUE, colour = 'black') +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = 'free_x', labeller = labeller(measure = measure_labels)) +
  labs(x = 'Imagery score', y = 'Memory MAE (degrees)')
imagery_association_plot
```

`r if (all(imagery_correlations[comparison != 'VVIQ – imagery/afterimage', p] >= .05)) 'Neither imagery measure showed a clear association with overall memory accuracy in this sample.' else 'The table shows which imagery measure was associated with overall memory accuracy and the direction of the association.'` These three correlations across the two imagery questions are exploratory and their p-values are unadjusted. Nonsignificant results leave uncertainty about the strength of the relationships.

## Does imagery ability predict the effect of noise?

For each person, we calculated how much their average error changed from low to high noise in the target patch. Positive changes mean that noise made memory less accurate. We then checked whether these changes were related to VVIQ scores or imagery/afterimage ratings. Other conditions were weighted equally in these comparisons.


As above, VVIQ associations use Pearson's correlation and imagery/afterimage associations use Spearman's correlation. The tables for these last two questions show both the original p-values and p-values adjusted with Holm's method across their four correlations. These analyses are exploratory.

```{r}
#| results: asis
knitr::kable(effect_correlations[effect != 'report_order', .(
  Comparison = unname(effect_labels[effect]),
  `Imagery measure` = unname(measure_labels[measure]), N = n,
  Correlation = round(estimate, 3), p = vapply(p, round_p, character(1), include.rel = FALSE),
  `Holm-adjusted p` = vapply(p_holm, round_p, character(1), include.rel = FALSE))])
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-imagery-noise-changes
#| fig-cap: "Imagery scores and changes in memory error when target noise increases. Each point is one participant. Positive changes mean worse memory with high noise. Lines and 95% confidence bands show descriptive linear fits."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-asp: 0.4

imagery_change_plot <- imagery_association_plot +
  aes(y = change) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = 'grey60')
imagery_change_plot %+% effect_pairs[effect == 'target_noise' & is.finite(imagery)] +
  labs(y = 'High-noise minus low-noise error (degrees)')
```

`r if (all(effect_correlations[effect != 'report_order', p_holm] >= .05, na.rm = TRUE)) 'Neither imagery measure clearly predicted the effect of noise after adjustment for the four correlations.' else 'At least one imagery measure was related to a noise effect after adjustment for the four correlations; the table identifies the measure and condition.'` The estimates and their uncertainty are shown in @fig-imagery-noise-changes. A nonsignificant result does not establish that imagery has no influence on sensitivity to noise.

## Does imagery ability predict the cost of reporting the second item?

We calculated each person's increase in average error from the first report to the second. Positive values mean that the second report was less accurate. Across participants, this increase was `r apa_mean_conf(report_changes$change)` degrees (`r apa(report_order_test)`).

We then asked whether imagery scores predicted this increase. A negative correlation would mean that people with stronger imagery lost less accuracy on their second report.

```{r}
#| results: asis
knitr::kable(effect_correlations[effect == 'report_order', .(
  `Imagery measure` = unname(measure_labels[measure]), N = n,
  Correlation = round(estimate, 3), p = vapply(p, round_p, character(1), include.rel = FALSE),
  `Holm-adjusted p` = vapply(p_holm, round_p, character(1), include.rel = FALSE))])
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-imagery-report-order-change
#| fig-cap: "Imagery scores and the increase in memory error from the first to the second report. Each point is one participant. Positive values mean a less accurate second report. Lines and 95% confidence bands show descriptive linear fits."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-asp: 0.4

imagery_change_plot %+% effect_pairs[effect == 'report_order' & is.finite(imagery)] +
  labs(y = 'Second-report minus first-report error (degrees)')
```

`r if (all(effect_correlations[effect == 'report_order', p_holm] >= .05, na.rm = TRUE)) 'Neither imagery measure clearly predicted the change from the first report to the second after adjustment for the four correlations.' else 'At least one imagery measure predicted the change from the first report to the second after adjustment for the four correlations; the table shows its direction.'` The sample leaves uncertainty about whether people with stronger imagery lose less accuracy on their second report.

The participant comparisons and their correlations are available in `imagery_condition_effects.csv` and `imagery_effect_correlations.csv`. All comparisons use the same outlier exclusions as the earlier accuracy analyses.

## Correlation matrix across all measures

The matrix brings together the five measures considered above: VVIQ, the imagery/afterimage rating, overall memory MAE, target-noise cost and second-report cost. Each point is a participant. Positive costs mean worse performance with high target noise or on the second report. The matrix repeats the earlier plots and also displays relationships between the memory measures.

Each panel uses participants with both measures available. The full table contains `r nrow(imagery_metrics)` sessions; missing imagery scores do not automatically exclude valid memory data, and memory exclusions do not remove valid imagery scores. The lines are descriptive, including for the ordinal afterimage rating.

```{r}
#| label: fig-imagery-correlations
#| fig-cap: "Scatterplot matrix of imagery measures, memory MAE, target-noise cost and second-report cost. Each off-diagonal panel shows one point per participant with both measures, an ordinary least-squares line and its 95% confidence band; diagonal panels show distributions. The regression lines are descriptive, including for the ordinal afterimage rating. Missing values are omitted separately for each pair."
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-asp: 1

smooth_panel <- list(continuous = GGally::wrap('smooth', method = 'lm', se = TRUE,
  colour = default_colors[1], alpha = 0.5, size = 1.7))
imagery_matrix <- GGally::ggpairs(as.data.frame(imagery_metrics),
  columns = c('vviq', 'afterimage_relative', 'memory_mae', 'target_noise_cost', 'report_order_cost'),
  columnLabels = c('VVIQ', 'Imagery /\nafterimage', 'Memory MAE\n(deg.)',
    'Target-noise\ncost (deg.)', 'Second-report\ncost (deg.)'),
  lower = smooth_panel, upper = smooth_panel,
  diag = list(continuous = 'densityDiag'), progress = FALSE) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10), axis.text = element_text(size = 8))
imagery_matrix

ggsave('imagery_correlation_matrix.png', imagery_matrix, width = 13, height = 13, dpi = 200, bg = 'white')
```

Participant scores and pairwise statistics are available in `imagery_participant_metrics.csv`, `imagery_correlations.csv`, `imagery_condition_effects.csv` and `imagery_effect_correlations.csv`.
